messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] high-429-rate detected for tenant fortress (prod-vpc-us-west-2). Route: /v1/generate. 429 spike sustained 5m. IncidentID: INC-2026-2512346789
maya_oncall: paging oncall, I'm here and looking.
sam_sre: sam_sre joining. I see per-tenant rate limiter at 100 RPS cap for fortress, counters saturated and backing off. Dedicated pool fortress-ded-1 is at 98% worker utilization.
carla_am: account side — customer (Fortress) reporting production errors in their app. They've escalated to our CS lead.
daniel_runtime: quick telemetry check: no upstream failures. It's token/quota exhaustion on our side. Control-plane shows tenant quota enforcement tripping.
maya_oncall: can we do an emergency reroute to a shared pool while we investigate? shared-dedicated-e2 has spare capacity and supports tenant isolation.
sam_sre: reroute possible but requires contract exception (traffic moves to shared hw). Need verbal ok from customer and a ticketed audit trail.
carla_am: customer ok on call for a short-term exception — they want service restored asap. I'm logging consent in support ticket.
lexi_support: created support/5678 with customer approval attached.
daniel_runtime: preparing control-plane override. Will post the exact API call here for transparency: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/api/v1/routing/overrides 
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OPS\" 
 -d '{"tenant":"fortress","from":"fortress-ded-1","to":"shared-dedicated-e2","duration_minutes":20,"reason":"emergency rate relief"}'
```
sam_sre: also recommend a transient policy to reduce token throughput: pin tenant to smaller model variant to lower per-request tokens. Proposal payload: 
```json
{"tenant":"fortress","model":"rtx-small","enforce_until":"2026-03-15T14:48:00Z"}
```
maya_oncall: executing routing override + policy now.
IncidentBot: Action queued: routing.override.create by maya_oncall.
maya_oncall: override applied. Control plane shows ~1.2k RPS diverted to shared-dedicated-e2. Monitoring ingress.
sam_sre: seeing immediate drop in 429s from 87% -> 24% in 90s. Model pin in effect, token volume down ~45%.
carla_am: notified customer: they confirm partial recovery, still seeing a handful of failures in edge region.
daniel_runtime: spinning up a 20% concurrency bump on fortress-ded-1 for deeper capacity while we root-cause. Also collecting per-worker traces.
lexi_support: attaching logs and call notes to support/5678 and linking to jira.
eva_legal: flag — we need a formal contract exception record within 24h. Please add details (who approved, time window, risk assessment).
maya_oncall: created JIRA RED-INC-9123 with audit, call recording URL, and exception details: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RED-INC-9123
sam_sre: dumping runtime logs to s3: `/s3/logs/incidents/2512346789/` — includes worker stderr, rate-limiter counters, and pprof snapshots.
maya_oncall: handing off monitoring to night oncall: @nate_oncall please keep an eye for recurrence. If 429 >5% for >10m escalate to eng-runtime.
nate_oncall: ack — monitoring. I've subscribed to the alert and set a 5m dashboard refresh.
carla_am: scheduling a 1h customer check-in to confirm stability and discuss a durable quota increase or contract amendment.
daniel_runtime: follow-ups: run post-mortem on why fortress-ded-1 didn't autoscale earlier; validate quota calc logic for multi-tenant pools; consider pre-warming for scheduled traffic.
maya_oncall: current metrics: 429 rate at 2%, latency normal. Will close once stable 30m. Great job team :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Incident marked mitigated by maya_oncall — monitoring window active.
maya_oncall: closing note: temporary reroute window 20m ended at override TTL; traffic returned to fortress-ded-1 after autoscale adjustments. Follow-ups assigned in RED-INC-9123 (owners: daniel_runtime, sam_sre, carla_am).
